system.summary: Lasry's 'TNA SP106-2' key (July-Aug 1645): a numerical homophonic alphabet on the numbers 1-60 (two values for most letters, nine for I), numbers separated by commas; a nomenclator of numbers above 60 (61-75, 97, 102-121) that his key file does not list.
system.sibling_key: Same key, per Lasry's files, on f. 219 (a letter of 30 Aug 1645 inside DECODE R788, ff. 218-221; the rest of R788 is in the TNA SP 106 key)
system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the former hm1645, which joined six letters in four of Lasry's keys. Lasry's key file lists only the letter values and says 'There are no nulls'. Other entries: hm1645 (TNA SP 106 key), sp106r924 (SP106-8), sp106r929 (SP106-5).

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE record page of R787 with the shared cookie; it links Pettersson's transcription, Lasry's reconstructed key 'TNA SP106-2' and his plaintext of ff. 216-217 and 219 (2020-10-23).

Re-fetched the record files and applied the key group by group to the 1569 groups of ff. 216-217 (apply_key.py): 1538 get a value, all equal to Lasry's plaintext (every line's columns line up); the 31 others are the numbers above 60 (and 9, 06) that his plaintext also leaves open.

Split from the former combined target hm1645 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R787 is the only letter of the six in the SP106-2 key. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; the earlier step is kept as recorded.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the DECODE record holding Pettersson's transcription and Lasry's plaintext; no local copy

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): Lasry's plaintext of R787 is on DECODE only (git-ignored copy in no checkout); nothing could be read. Relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved kept (Lasry's decipherment); fraction_read 0.9802 -> 0.

outcome.method_basis: The letter was taken from George Lasry's plaintext on the DECODE record (23 Oct 2020); his SP106-2 key, applied here only as a check, reproduces it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit, 22 Oct 2026: the letter's text is not in the repository (Lasry's files were git-ignored and are in no checkout), so no tokens are in a document that reads here. The earlier 0.9802 (apply_key.py: 1538 of 1569 groups with a value in Lasry's key) is withdrawn as a reading figure.

gaps.item: nomenclator numbers above 60 (61-75, 83, 97, 102-121) and two stray figures (9, 06): 19 distinct, 31 tokens
gaps.detail: Not in Lasry's key; his plaintext brackets them or marks them '?'. Mostly names and titles (64 recurs five times as a party or person). The signature 103 62 A 104 is among them.

gaps.item: R787: Lasry's plaintext not in the repository
gaps.detail: his interlinear and plaintext files are on the DECODE record (reachable with the shared DECODE cookie (targets/bordeaux/decode/cookie.txt)); fetch them into decode/ (git-ignored, his work), grade them as sentences, and ask him whether a reading copy may be kept

outcome.notes: Nothing about the text is new: Lasry's decipherment on DECODE is the reading. Lasry dates it from its war news (Linck, Piccolomini, Enghien, Montrose, the Parlement and the duc d'Epernon) to summer 1645 and suggests it may be Goffe's letter from Holland forwarded unchanged. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no text of the letter is in the repository; decoded, not read. Class kept: Lasry's decipherment exists on DECODE (2020).

credits.note: reconstructed key 'TNA SP106-2' (July-Aug 1645) and interlinear plaintext of R787, with dating notes

texts.label: R787, 19/29 July 1645
texts.summary: A French news letter (a duplicate) forwarded to Henrietta Maria's household: the Parlement de Paris and the duc d'Épernon, an envoy refusing to be heard except as ambassador, Enghien taking Heidelberg, the fort of Linck taken, Piccolomini entrenched round Dunkirk, a check to Montrose.
texts.note: Lasry's interlinear plaintext of R787 is on the DECODE record, behind its login, and was kept out of the repository as his work; no copy is in any checkout, so nothing of the letter can be read here (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026); fix: re-fetch it with the shared DECODE cookie (targets/bordeaux/decode/cookie.txt) and check it with apply_key.py.
